CHAPTER 25 — परियोजना-निर्माणम् (PARIYOJANA-NIRMANAM)

Introduction — परियोजना किम्?

The word परियोजना (pariyojana) is formed from परि (pari = around, thoroughly) + योजना (yojana = planning, arrangement, from the root युज् 'to join'). A परियोजना is therefore a 'thorough plan' — what we call a PROJECT in English: a piece of independent study in which the learner chooses a topic, gathers material, arranges it, writes a report and presents it. In senior secondary Sanskrit study, परियोजना-निर्माणम् (project-making) is a skills lesson: instead of only reading what others have written, the student becomes a small researcher (अनुसन्धाता) who explores Sanskrit language, literature and culture in his or her own surroundings. छात्रः स्वयं विषयं चिनोति, सामग्रीं संगृह्णाति, प्रतिवेदनं लिखति, प्रस्तुतिं च करोति। (The student personally chooses a topic, collects material, writes a report, and makes a presentation.)

Why project work matters (परियोजनायाः महत्त्वम्)

A project turns passive reading into active learning. परियोजनया छात्रस्य ज्ञानं स्थिरं भवति। (Through a project the student's knowledge becomes firm.) It builds four abilities at once: (1) स्वाध्यायः — independent study and reading of sources; (2) अनुसन्धानम् — inquiry: asking questions, observing, interviewing; (3) लेखनकौशलम् — the skill of organised writing in simple Sanskrit; (4) प्रस्तुतिकौशलम् — the confidence to present findings before a group. A project also connects the classroom to the community: temples, inscriptions, festivals, proverbs, plants and rivers of one's own village become material for Sanskrit study. NIOS learners submit projects as part of assessment, so knowing the METHOD of project-making is as important as the content.

The six steps of परियोजना-निर्माणम् (षट् सोपानानि)

STEP 1 — विषयचयनम् (Choosing the topic). प्रथमं सोपानं विषयचयनम् अस्ति। Choose a topic that is (a) रुचिकरः — interesting to YOU; (b) सीमितः — limited and manageable, not too broad; (c) साधनसुलभः — one for which sources are actually available near you; (d) संस्कृत-सम्बद्धः — connected with Sanskrit language or culture. 'संस्कृतसाहित्यम्' (the whole of Sanskrit literature) is far too broad; 'मम ग्रामस्य मन्दिराणि' (the temples of my village) is limited, local and doable. Write the chosen title clearly: शीर्षकम् स्पष्टं लघु च भवेत्। (The title should be clear and short.)

STEP 2 — सामग्रीसंग्रहः (Collecting the material). द्वितीयं सोपानं सामग्रीसंग्रहः। Material (सामग्री) comes from three kinds of sources (स्रोतांसि): (1) ग्रन्थाः — books, textbooks, dictionaries (शब्दकोशाः), magazines and reliable web pages; note down each source for the सन्दर्भसूची (bibliography). (2) साक्षात्कारः — interviews: prepare a short प्रश्नावली (questionnaire) and politely question knowledgeable people — a priest (पुरोहितः), a teacher (अध्यापकः), elders (वृद्धाः). अहं ग्रामस्य वृद्धान् अपृच्छम्। (I asked the elders of the village.) (3) क्षेत्रभ्रमणम् — field visits: go to the place itself (temple, river bank, library), observe (निरीक्षणं करोति), take notes (टिप्पणीः लिखति) and, with permission, photographs (चित्राणि). Always record WHERE and WHEN each piece of information was found.

STEP 3 — विषयविभाजनम् / रूपरेखा (Dividing the subject; the outline). तृतीयं सोपानं विषयविभाजनम्। Divide the big topic into 4–6 small sections (अंशाः) and arrange them in a logical order — this ordered list is the रूपरेखा (outline). A standard रूपरेखा has: शीर्षकम् (title) → प्रस्तावना (introduction) → मध्यभागः विभागशः (the middle, section by section) → निष्कर्षः (conclusion) → सन्दर्भसूची (list of sources). रूपरेखा मार्गदर्शिका इव अस्ति। (The outline is like a guide-map.) A good outline prevents repetition and shows at a glance what is missing.

STEP 4 — प्रतिवेदनलेखनम् (Writing the report). चतुर्थं सोपानं प्रतिवेदनलेखनम्। Now write the report (प्रतिवेदनम्) following the outline: simple, correct Sanskrit sentences; short paragraphs, one section per heading; where needed, tables, lists and pictures with captions. Begin with a प्रस्तावना stating the aim (उद्देश्यम्) and method (विधिः); end with a निष्कर्षः stating what was learnt; attach the सन्दर्भसूची. लेखनं शुद्धं सरलं च भवेत्। (The writing should be correct and simple.) Revise (संशोधनं करोति) at least once: check spelling, sandhi and case endings.

STEP 5 — प्रस्तुतिः (Presentation). पञ्चमं सोपानं प्रस्तुतिः। Present the project before the class or teacher: speak slowly and clearly (मन्दं स्पष्टं च वदेत्), show the main points on a chart (सूचनापटः) or slides, recite one or two Sanskrit lines from the project, and answer questions (प्रश्नानाम् उत्तराणि ददाति) politely. A presentation is not reading the whole report aloud — it is telling its ESSENCE (सारः) in a few minutes.

STEP 6 — मूल्याङ्कनम् (Evaluation). षष्ठं सोपानं मूल्याङ्कनम्। The project is judged (मूल्याङ्कनं भवति) on: topic choice and originality (मौलिकता), quality and variety of sources, order and completeness of the outline, correctness of language, neatness, and the presentation. Self-evaluation first: किम् उद्देश्यं सिद्धम्? (Was the aim achieved?) किं सर्वे स्रोताः निर्दिष्टाः? (Are all sources cited?)

Three worked example outlines (आदर्श-रूपरेखाः)

EXAMPLE 1 — मम ग्रामस्य मन्दिराणि (The temples of my village).
उद्देश्यम्: स्वग्रामस्य मन्दिराणां परिचयः संस्कृतेन लेखनम् च। (Aim: an introduction to my village's temples, written in Sanskrit.)
रूपरेखा: (1) प्रस्तावना — ग्रामस्य नाम स्थानं च; (2) मन्दिराणां सूची — नामानि देवताः च; (3) प्रमुखं मन्दिरम् — इतिहासः, शिल्पम्, अभिलेखाः; (4) उत्सवाः — के उत्सवाः कदा भवन्ति; (5) साक्षात्कारः — पुरोहितस्य वृद्धानां च वचनानि; (6) निष्कर्षः सन्दर्भसूची च।
Method: field visit to each temple (क्षेत्रभ्रमणम्), interview of the priest (साक्षात्कारः), photographs, and any old records. English note: this project practises observation and description — writing simple sentences like 'ग्रामस्य मध्ये शिवमन्दिरम् अस्ति। तत्र महाशिवरात्रौ महान् उत्सवः भवति।'

EXAMPLE 2 — संस्कृतसुभाषितसंग्रहः (A collection of Sanskrit subhashitas).
उद्देश्यम्: विषयानुसारं पञ्चविंशतिः सुभाषितानां संग्रहः अर्थलेखनं च। (Aim: to collect 25 subhashitas theme-wise and write their meanings.)
रूपरेखा: (1) प्रस्तावना — सुभाषितं किम्?; (2) विद्याविषयकाणि सुभाषितानि; (3) उद्यमविषयकाणि; (4) सदाचारविषयकाणि; (5) प्रत्येकं सुभाषितस्य अर्थः सन्देशः च; (6) निष्कर्षः सन्दर्भसूची च।
Method: library work with books of subhashitas (ग्रन्थाः एव मुख्यं स्रोतः), grouping by theme, writing each verse with its meaning in simple Sanskrit and English. English note: this project practises classification (वर्गीकरणम्) and translation; the 'field' here is the library.

EXAMPLE 3 — पर्यावरणसंरक्षणे वृक्षाणां महत्त्वम् (The importance of trees in environmental protection).
उद्देश्यम्: वृक्षाणाम् उपकाराणां वर्णनं, वृक्षारोपणस्य प्रेरणा च। (Aim: to describe the benefits of trees and inspire tree-planting.)
रूपरेखा: (1) प्रस्तावना — पर्यावरणसमस्या; (2) वृक्षाणाम् उपकाराः — छाया फलं शुद्धवायुः वृष्टिः च; (3) संस्कृतवाङ्मये वृक्षाः — वृक्षविषयकाणि वचनानि; (4) क्षेत्रनिरीक्षणम् — विद्यालयपरिसरस्य वृक्षाणां सूची; (5) वृक्षारोपणयोजना; (6) निष्कर्षः सन्दर्भसूची च।
Method: combine book sources with a field count of trees near the school, and end with an action plan. English note: this project joins language work to an environmental value — परोपकाराय फलन्ति वृक्षाः is its guiding idea.

Tips (उपयोगिनः सङ्केताः) and common mistakes (सामान्यदोषाः)

TIPS: (1) Start early; a project is done क्रमेण (step by step), not in one night. (2) Keep a project diary (परियोजना-पञ्जिका) and write notes the same day. (3) Prefer what you can SEE and ASK over what you can only copy. (4) Keep Sanskrit sentences short — कर्ता, कर्म, क्रिया। (5) Read the report aloud once; the ear catches errors the eye misses. (6) Number pages, sections and pictures.
COMMON MISTAKES: (1) अतिविस्तृतः विषयः — choosing a topic too broad to finish. (2) Copying pages from a book without understanding — that is प्रतिलिपिः (copying), not अनुसन्धानम्; always write in your own words and cite the source. (3) No रूपरेखा — writing without an outline produces disorder and repetition. (4) Missing सन्दर्भसूची — sources not listed. (5) Ignoring revision — submitting the first draft with sandhi and विभक्ति errors. (6) Reading the whole report aloud in the presentation instead of telling its essence.

व्याकरणम् — Language of the project process (English explanation, Devanagari examples)

(A) Process nouns (ल्युट्-प्रत्ययान्ताः शब्दाः). Many step-names are neuter action-nouns formed with the suffix -अन (ल्युट्): चयनम् (choosing, from चि 'to gather'), लेखनम् (writing, from लिख्), विभाजनम् (dividing, from वि+भज्), भ्रमणम् (touring, from भ्रम्), निरीक्षणम् (observing), मूल्याङ्कनम् (evaluating, मूल्य + अङ्कनम् 'marking the value'). Others are formed differently: संग्रहः (collection, सम् + ग्रह्, masculine), प्रस्तुतिः (presentation, feminine -ति), रूपरेखा (outline, 'form-line', feminine), प्रतिवेदनम् (report), प्रश्नावली (questionnaire, प्रश्न + आवली 'row of questions'), सन्दर्भसूची (bibliography, 'list of references').

(B) कृदन्त forms in project sentences. (1) क्त्वा (having done): विषयं चित्वा छात्रः सामग्रीं संगृह्णाति। (Having chosen the topic, the student collects material.) सामग्रीं संगृह्य सः रूपरेखां रचयति। (Having collected the material, he composes the outline.) प्रतिवेदनं लिखित्वा सा प्रस्तुतिं करोति। (Having written the report, she makes the presentation.) (2) तुमुन् (in order to): सामग्रीं संग्रहीतुं छात्रः ग्रन्थालयं गच्छति। (To collect material the student goes to the library.) वृद्धान् प्रष्टुं सः ग्रामं गच्छति। (He goes to the village to question the elders.) (3) क्त past participle: चितः विषयः (the chosen topic), लिखितं प्रतिवेदनम् (the written report), संगृहीता सामग्री (the collected material).

(C) विभक्ति usage in the process. तृतीया (by/with): प्रश्नावल्या साक्षात्कारं करोति (conducts the interview WITH a questionnaire); लेखन्या टिप्पणीं लिखति (writes notes WITH a pen). पञ्चमी (from): ग्रन्थेभ्यः सामग्रीं गृह्णाति (takes material FROM books); पुरोहितात् वार्तां शृणोति (hears the account FROM the priest). सप्तमी (in/at): प्रस्तुतौ मन्दं वदेत् (in the presentation one should speak slowly); ग्रन्थालये पठति (reads IN the library); रूपरेखायां षट् अंशाः सन्ति (in the outline there are six sections). षष्ठी (of): परियोजनायाः शीर्षकम् (the title OF the project); मन्दिरस्य इतिहासः (the history OF the temple).

SUMMARY (सारांश)

In this chapter you learned that a परियोजना (परि + योजना, a thorough plan) is a piece of independent study, and that परियोजना-निर्माणम् proceeds in six steps: विषयचयनम् (choose a limited, interesting, source-rich topic), सामग्रीसंग्रहः (collect material from books, interviews and field visits, noting every source), विषयविभाजनम्/रूपरेखा (divide the subject and fix an outline from प्रस्तावना to सन्दर्भसूची), प्रतिवेदनलेखनम् (write a simple, correct, revised report), प्रस्तुतिः (present the essence clearly and answer questions), and मूल्याङ्कनम् (evaluation of originality, sources, order, language and presentation). Three model outlines — मम ग्रामस्य मन्दिराणि, संस्कृतसुभाषितसंग्रहः, and पर्यावरणसंरक्षणे वृक्षाणां महत्त्वम् — showed how the method works in practice. You also learned the process vocabulary, the कृदन्त forms (चित्वा, संगृह्य, लिखित्वा; संग्रहीतुम्; चितः, लिखितम्) and the विभक्ति usage (तृतीया of means, पञ्चमी of source, सप्तमी of place, षष्ठी of relation) that make project Sanskrit flow naturally.

bullets: परियोजना = परि (thoroughly) + योजना (planning): a thorough plan — a project in which the learner studies one topic independently from choice to presentation.
Project work turns passive reading into active learning: the student becomes a small researcher (अनुसन्धाता) exploring Sanskrit in his or her own surroundings.
It builds four abilities together — स्वाध्यायः (independent study), अनुसन्धानम् (inquiry), लेखनकौशलम् (organised writing) and प्रस्तुतिकौशलम् (presentation).
NIOS learners submit projects for assessment, so the METHOD of project-making matters as much as the content.

sections.heading: Choosing the topic and collecting material (steps 1–2)
bullets: विषयचयनम्: the topic must be रुचिकर (interesting), सीमित (limited), साधनसुलभ (source-rich) and संस्कृत-सम्बद्ध; 'संस्कृतसाहित्यम्' is too broad, 'मम ग्रामस्य मन्दिराणि' is doable.
सामग्रीसंग्रहः draws on three kinds of sources: ग्रन्थाः (books, dictionaries, articles), साक्षात्कारः (interviews) and क्षेत्रभ्रमणम् (field visits).
For interviews prepare a प्रश्नावली (questionnaire) and question knowledgeable people politely; on field visits observe (निरीक्षणम्) and write notes (टिप्पणी) the same day.
Record where and when each piece of information was found — it all goes into the सन्दर्भसूची (bibliography).

sections.heading: Outline and report (steps 3–4)
bullets: विषयविभाजनम्: divide the topic into 4–6 small ordered sections (अंशाः); the ordered list is the रूपरेखा (outline), a guide-map that prevents repetition.
The standard रूपरेखा runs: शीर्षकम् → प्रस्तावना → मध्यभागः (section by section) → निष्कर्षः → सन्दर्भसूची.
प्रतिवेदनलेखनम्: write simple correct Sanskrit following the outline — short paragraphs, one section per heading, tables and pictures with captions.
State the aim (उद्देश्यम्) and method (विधिः) in the प्रस्तावना, state what was learnt in the निष्कर्षः, and revise once for spelling, sandhi and case endings.

sections.heading: Presentation and evaluation (steps 5–6)
bullets: प्रस्तुतिः is telling the ESSENCE (सारः) of the project in a few minutes — not reading the whole report aloud.
Speak slowly and clearly (मन्दं स्पष्टं च वदेत्), use a chart or slides, recite a Sanskrit line or two, and answer questions politely.
मूल्याङ्कनम् judges topic choice and originality (मौलिकता), sources, order and completeness of the outline, correctness of language, neatness and presentation.
Self-evaluate first: किम् उद्देश्यं सिद्धम्? (Was the aim achieved?) किं सर्वे स्रोताः निर्दिष्टाः? (Are all sources cited?)

sections.heading: Model projects, common mistakes and grammar
bullets: मम ग्रामस्य मन्दिराणि uses field visits and a priest's interview; संस्कृतसुभाषितसंग्रहः is library work with theme-wise classification; पर्यावरणसंरक्षणे वृक्षाणां महत्त्वम् joins book sources to a field count of trees.

Common mistakes: an over-broad topic, copying without understanding (प्रतिलिपिः, not अनुसन्धानम्), no रूपरेखा, missing सन्दर्भसूची, skipping revision, and reading the whole report aloud in the presentation.
Process nouns name the steps: चयनम्, संग्रहः, विभाजनम्, लेखनम्, प्रस्तुतिः, मूल्याङ्कनम्; कृदन्त forms chain the actions — विषयं चित्वा, सामग्रीं संगृह्य, लिखित्वा; संग्रहीतुम्.
विभक्ति usage: तृतीया for means (प्रश्नावल्या), पञ्चमी for source (ग्रन्थेभ्यः), सप्तमी for place (प्रस्तुतौ, ग्रन्थालये), षष्ठी for relation (परियोजनायाः शीर्षकम्).

key_takeaways: A परियोजना (परि + योजना) is a thorough plan — an independent study project carried from topic choice to presentation by the learner.
परियोजना-निर्माणम् has six steps in order: विषयचयनम्, सामग्रीसंग्रहः, विषयविभाजनम्/रूपरेखा, प्रतिवेदनलेखनम्, प्रस्तुतिः, मूल्याङ्कनम्.
A good topic is interesting, limited, source-rich and Sanskrit-related; a good title is short and clear.
Material comes from ग्रन्थाः, साक्षात्कारः and क्षेत्रभ्रमणम् — and every source must be recorded in the सन्दर्भसूची.
The रूपरेखा (शीर्षकम् → प्रस्तावना → sections → निष्कर्षः → सन्दर्भसूची) is the guide-map of the report; write simple correct Sanskrit and revise.
Presentation means telling the essence clearly, not reading the report; evaluation weighs originality, sources, order, language and delivery.
Project Sanskrit uses क्त्वा chains (विषयं चित्वा सामग्रीं संगृह्य प्रतिवेदनं लिखति) and clear विभक्ति roles — तृतीया by, पञ्चमी from, सप्तमी in, षष्ठी of.

glossary.definition: A project — a thorough plan (परि + योजना): independent study of one topic carried through choice, collection, outline, report and presentation.
Topic selection; the first step — choosing an interesting, limited, source-rich, Sanskrit-related subject.
Collection of material; gathering information from books, interviews and field visits.
Interview; questioning a knowledgeable person face to face using a prepared questionnaire.
Field visit; going to the place itself to observe, take notes and gather first-hand information.
Questionnaire; a prepared row of questions (प्रश्न + आवली) used in interviews.
Division of the subject into small ordered sections before writing.
Outline ('form-line'); the ordered plan of the report from प्रस्तावना to सन्दर्भसूची.
Introduction; the opening section stating the aim (उद्देश्यम्) and method (विधिः) of the project.
Report; the written account of the project composed section by section following the outline.
Conclusion; the closing section stating what was found and learnt.
Bibliography; the list of all sources — books, persons interviewed, places visited — used in the project.
Presentation; telling the essence of the project clearly before a group and answering questions.
Evaluation; judging the project on originality, sources, order, language, neatness and presentation.
Inquiry or research; finding out by one's own questions, observation and study — the opposite of mere copying (प्रतिलिपिः).

worksheet.title: Worksheet — परियोजना-निर्माणम् (NIOS Sanskrit 309, Chapter 25)
worksheet.instructions: Attempt all questions. Write Sanskrit words in Devanagari and give your explanations in English. Refer to the six steps and the model outlines in the lesson where needed.

questions.question: Name the six steps (षट् सोपानानि) of परियोजना-निर्माणम् in the correct order, in Sanskrit.
questions.answer: 1. विषयचयनम् (choosing the topic), 2. सामग्रीसंग्रहः (collecting material), 3. विषयविभाजनम्/रूपरेखा-निर्माणम् (dividing the subject and making the outline), 4. प्रतिवेदनलेखनम् (writing the report), 5. प्रस्तुतिः (presentation), 6. मूल्याङ्कनम् (evaluation).
questions.explanation: The fixed order of the six steps is the backbone of the chapter.

questions.question: State the four qualities of a good project topic (विषयः) with their Sanskrit terms.
questions.answer: A good topic is (1) रुचिकरः — interesting to the student; (2) सीमितः — limited and manageable, not too broad; (3) साधनसुलभः — one for which sources are available nearby; (4) संस्कृत-सम्बद्धः — connected with Sanskrit language or culture.
questions.explanation: These four criteria decide whether a project can actually be completed well.

questions.question: Name the three kinds of sources (स्रोतांसि) for सामग्रीसंग्रहः and give one example of each.
questions.answer: (1) ग्रन्थाः — books and written sources, e.g. a dictionary (शब्दकोशः) or a book of subhashitas; (2) साक्षात्कारः — interviews, e.g. questioning the temple priest (पुरोहितः) with a प्रश्नावली; (3) क्षेत्रभ्रमणम् — field visits, e.g. visiting the village temple and taking notes (टिप्पणी).
questions.explanation: Books, interviews and field visits are the three pillars of material collection.

questions.question: Write the five parts of a standard रूपरेखा in order, from title to bibliography.
questions.answer: शीर्षकम् (title) → प्रस्तावना (introduction) → मध्यभागः विभागशः (the middle, section by section) → निष्कर्षः (conclusion) → सन्दर्भसूची (bibliography).
questions.explanation: The outline is the guide-map of the report; its order prevents disorder and repetition.

questions.question: Give the meaning and grammatical role: (a) प्रश्नावल्या (b) ग्रन्थेभ्यः (c) प्रस्तुतौ.
questions.answer: (a) प्रश्नावल्या = 'with/by the questionnaire' — तृतीया (instrumental) of प्रश्नावली. (b) ग्रन्थेभ्यः = 'from the books' — पञ्चमी (ablative) plural of ग्रन्थः. (c) प्रस्तुतौ = 'in the presentation' — सप्तमी (locative) of प्रस्तुतिः.
questions.explanation: तृतीया shows means, पञ्चमी shows source, सप्तमी shows place — the three key cases of project language.

questions.question: You are given the project 'मम ग्रामस्य मन्दिराणि'. Write its aim (उद्देश्यम्) in one Sanskrit sentence and construct a full रूपरेखा of six parts. Then state in English which two sources you would mainly use and why.
questions.answer:
उद्देश्यम्: स्वग्रामस्य मन्दिराणां परिचयः संस्कृतेन लेखनम् च। (To introduce the temples of my own village and write about them in Sanskrit.)
रूपरेखा: (1) प्रस्तावना — ग्रामस्य नाम स्थानं च; (2) मन्दिराणां सूची — नामानि देवताः च; (3) प्रमुखं मन्दिरम् — इतिहासः शिल्पम् अभिलेखाः च; (4) उत्सवाः — के उत्सवाः कदा भवन्ति; (5) साक्षात्कारः — पुरोहितस्य वृद्धानां च वचनानि; (6) निष्कर्षः सन्दर्भसूची च।
Main sources: (1) क्षेत्रभ्रमणम् — visiting each temple to observe the buildings, images and inscriptions first-hand, because the topic is local and no book describes these temples fully; (2) साक्षात्कारः — interviewing the priest and village elders with a prepared प्रश्नावली, because they hold the history and festival details that are nowhere written down.
questions.explanation: A local-heritage project rests on field observation and interviews, organised by a six-part outline.

questions.question: Write four simple Sanskrit sentences (in Devanagari) describing the steps a student takes while making a project, using at least two क्त्वा/ल्यप् forms (e.g. चित्वा, संगृह्य, लिखित्वा). Give the English meaning of each sentence.
questions.answer:
1. छात्रः प्रथमं रुचिकरं विषयं चिनोति। (First the student chooses an interesting topic.)
2. विषयं चित्वा सः ग्रन्थेभ्यः सामग्रीं संगृह्णाति। (Having chosen the topic, he collects material from books.)
3. सामग्रीं संगृह्य सः रूपरेखां रचयति प्रतिवेदनं च लिखति। (Having collected the material, he composes the outline and writes the report.)
4. प्रतिवेदनं लिखित्वा सः कक्षायां प्रस्तुतिं करोति। (Having written the report, he makes the presentation in class.)
questions.explanation: क्त्वा/ल्यप् forms (चित्वा, संगृह्य, लिखित्वा) chain the project steps into flowing Sanskrit narrative.

questions.question: List any four criteria on which a project is evaluated (मूल्याङ्कनम्).
questions.answer: Any four of: (1) topic choice and originality (मौलिकता); (2) quality and variety of sources; (3) order and completeness of the रूपरेखा; (4) correctness of language (शुद्धिः); (5) neatness; (6) quality of the प्रस्तुतिः including answering questions.
questions.explanation: Evaluation looks at the whole journey — choice, sources, order, language and delivery.

questions.question: Why is copying pages from a book NOT acceptable in a project? What should the student do instead?
questions.answer: Copying pages without understanding is प्रतिलिपिः (mere copying), not अनुसन्धानम् (inquiry); it shows no learning and hides the real sources. Instead the student should read the source, understand it, write the matter in his or her OWN simple Sanskrit words, and cite the book in the सन्दर्भसूची.
questions.explanation: A project rewards inquiry and one's own expression, with honest citation of sources.

questions.question: The topic 'संस्कृतसाहित्यम्' (Sanskrit literature) was rejected for a class project, but 'संस्कृतसुभाषितसंग्रहः' was accepted. Explain why, using the criteria of topic choice.
questions.answer: 'संस्कृतसाहित्यम्' is अतिविस्तृतः — far too broad; the whole of Sanskrit literature cannot be covered in one project, and no clear outline is possible. 'संस्कृतसुभाषितसंग्रहः' is सीमितः (limited — e.g. 25 verses grouped by theme), साधनसुलभः (books of subhashitas are easily available) and clearly संस्कृत-सम्बद्धः, so it can be finished well.
questions.explanation: A manageable, source-rich, clearly bounded topic beats a grand but impossible one.

questions.explanation: Language correctness — वर्तनी, सन्धि, विभक्ति — is a key evaluation point.

questions.question: 'उद्देश्यम्' means
questions.explanation: The प्रस्तावना states the उद्देश्यम् (aim) of the project.

questions.question: In which part of the report does the student state what was learnt?
questions.explanation: The conclusion sums up findings and learning.

questions.question: 'लेखनं शुद्धं सरलं च भवेत्' means
options: the writing should be correct and simple
the writing should be long and loud
the writing should be in verse only
questions.answer: the writing should be correct and simple
questions.explanation: शुद्ध = correct/pure; सरल = simple; भवेत् = should be.

questions.question: Tables, lists and pictures in the report should be given
questions.explanation: Number pages, sections and pictures, and caption every figure.

questions.question: Which Sanskrit sentence is fittest for the प्रस्तावना of the subhashita project?
options: मम परियोजनायाः उद्देश्यं सुभाषितानां संग्रहः अर्थलेखनं च अस्ति।
questions.answer: मम परियोजनायाः उद्देश्यं सुभाषितानां संग्रहः अर्थलेखनं च अस्ति।
questions.explanation: The introduction must state the project's aim; the other sentences are irrelevant.

questions.question: 'प्रस्तुतिः' means
questions.explanation: प्रस्तुतिः = presenting the project before a group.

questions.question: A good प्रस्तुतिः tells the ____ of the project in a few minutes.
questions.explanation: Presentation is the essence, not a full reading of the report.

questions.question: 'मन्दं स्पष्टं च वदेत्' advises the presenter to speak
questions.explanation: मन्दम् = slowly; स्पष्टम् = clearly; वदेत् = one should speak.

questions.question: 'सूचनापटः' used in a presentation means a
questions.explanation: Main points are shown on a chart (सूचनापटः) or slides.

questions.question: 'मूल्याङ्कनम्' means
questions.explanation: मूल्य (value) + अङ्कनम् (marking) = evaluation.

questions.question: 'मौलिकता', one criterion of evaluation, means
questions.explanation: Original, self-done work scores; copied work does not.

questions.question: During his presentation a student reads the entire 20-page report aloud. This is
options: a mistake — he should present only the essence
questions.answer: a mistake — he should present only the essence
questions.explanation: Reading the whole report aloud is listed among the common mistakes.

questions.question: The self-evaluation question 'किम् उद्देश्यं सिद्धम्?' asks
questions.explanation: उद्देश्यम् = aim; सिद्धम् = accomplished.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT an evaluation criterion mentioned in the lesson?
options: order and completeness of the outline
questions.explanation: Evaluation weighs choice, sources, order, language, neatness and delivery — not expense.

questions.question: The process noun 'चयनम्' (from the root चि) means
questions.explanation: चि 'to gather/select' + -अन (ल्युट्) = चयनम्, selection.

questions.question: Process nouns like लेखनम्, चयनम्, विभाजनम् are formed with which suffix?
questions.explanation: ल्युट् forms neuter action-nouns in -अन: लेखनम् 'writing', चयनम् 'choosing'.

questions.question: 'संग्रहः' means
questions.explanation: सम् + ग्रह् = gathering together, collection.

questions.question: The क्त्वा (gerund) form of लिख् 'to write' is
questions.explanation: लिखित्वा = 'having written'; तुमुन् would be लेखितुम्, क्त is लिखितम्.

questions.question: 'विषयं चित्वा' means
options: in order to choose the topic
questions.explanation: चित्वा is the क्त्वा form: 'having chosen'.

questions.question: Fill the तुमुन् form: 'सामग्रीं ____ छात्रः ग्रन्थालयं गच्छति।' (To collect material the student goes to the library.)
questions.explanation: तुमुन् (-तुम्) expresses purpose: संग्रहीतुम् 'in order to collect'.

questions.question: In 'लिखितं प्रतिवेदनम्' (the written report), लिखित is a
questions.explanation: क्त forms adjectives of completed action: लिखित 'written', चित 'chosen'.

questions.question: In 'प्रश्नावल्या साक्षात्कारं करोति', the word प्रश्नावल्या is in which विभक्ति?
questions.explanation: 'WITH the questionnaire' — the means, hence तृतीया.

questions.question: 'ग्रन्थेभ्यः सामग्रीं गृह्णाति' means the student takes material
questions.explanation: ग्रन्थेभ्यः is पञ्चमी plural — 'from the books', the source.

questions.question: In 'प्रस्तुतौ मन्दं वदेत्', the word प्रस्तुतौ is in which विभक्ति?
questions.explanation: 'IN the presentation' — place/occasion, hence सप्तमी of प्रस्तुतिः.

questions.question: In 'परियोजनायाः शीर्षकम्' (the title of the project), the षष्ठी ending shows
questions.explanation: षष्ठी marks the 'of' relation between project and title.

questions.question: 'प्रश्नावली' literally means a
questions.explanation: प्रश्न (question) + आवली (row/series).

questions.question: The main sources for the project 'मम ग्रामस्य मन्दिराणि' are
questions.explanation: A local-heritage topic needs first-hand observation and the priest's/elders' accounts.

questions.question: For 'संस्कृतसुभाषितसंग्रहः', the MAIN source of material is
questions.explanation: ग्रन्थाः एव मुख्यं स्रोतः — the 'field' of this project is the library.

questions.question: In the model outline, how many subhashitas does the संग्रह project aim to collect?
questions.explanation: पञ्चविंशतिः सुभाषितानां संग्रहः — 25 verses, grouped by theme.

questions.question: The guiding idea of the tree project 'पर्यावरणसंरक्षणे वृक्षाणां महत्त्वम्' is the line
questions.explanation: 'Trees bear fruit for the good of others' guides the environmental project.

questions.question: In the tree project, book sources are combined with which field activity?
options: counting and listing the trees near the school
questions.answer: counting and listing the trees near the school
questions.explanation: क्षेत्रनिरीक्षणम् — a field survey of the school campus trees.

questions.question: 'वर्गीकरणम्', practised in the subhashita project, means
questions.explanation: Verses are grouped theme-wise: विद्या, उद्यम, सदाचार.

questions.question: Which model project ends with an action plan (वृक्षारोपणयोजना)?
questions.explanation: The tree project closes with a tree-planting plan, joining study to action.

questions.question: परियोजना means a project — a thorough plan (परि + योजना).
questions.explanation: परि (thoroughly) + योजना (planning).

questions.question: In परियोजना-निर्माणम्, evaluation (मूल्याङ्कनम्) is done FIRST, before choosing the topic.
questions.explanation: विषयचयनम् is the first step; मूल्याङ्कनम् is the last.

questions.question: The broader a project topic is, the better the project will be.
questions.explanation: A topic must be सीमित (limited); over-broad topics cannot be finished well.

questions.question: साक्षात्कारः means an interview conducted face to face with a knowledgeable person.
questions.explanation: साक्षात् = face to face; interviews use a prepared प्रश्नावली.

questions.question: Only printed books count as sources; interviews and field visits are not sources.
questions.explanation: ग्रन्थाः, साक्षात्कारः and क्षेत्रभ्रमणम् are all valid sources.

questions.question: In the standard रूपरेखा, the निष्कर्षः (conclusion) comes before the प्रस्तावना (introduction).
questions.explanation: The order is शीर्षकम् → प्रस्तावना → middle → निष्कर्षः → सन्दर्भसूची.

questions.question: The first draft of the report should be submitted without any revision (संशोधनम्).
questions.explanation: Revise at least once — check spelling, sandhi and case endings.

questions.question: A good presentation means reading the whole report aloud word by word.
questions.explanation: Presentation means telling the essence (सारः) in a few minutes.

questions.question: The words चयनम्, लेखनम् and विभाजनम् are action-nouns formed with the suffix -अन (ल्युट्).
questions.explanation: ल्युट् forms neuter process nouns: choosing, writing, dividing.

questions.question: For the project 'संस्कृतसुभाषितसंग्रहः', the library is the main 'field' of work.
questions.explanation: Books of subhashitas are the chief source; the work is collection and classification.

questions.question: परियोजना = परि + ____।
questions.explanation: परि (thoroughly) + योजना (planning) = project.

questions.question: Complete: 'द्वितीयं सोपानं ____ अस्ति।' (The second step is material collection.)
questions.explanation: After topic choice comes सामग्रीसंग्रहः.

questions.question: Complete: 'प्रथमं सोपानं ____ अस्ति।' (The first step is topic selection.)
questions.explanation: विषयचयनम् — choosing the topic — comes first.

questions.question: Complete: 'शीर्षकम् स्पष्टं ____ च भवेत्।' (The title should be clear and short.)
questions.explanation: लघु = short; the title should be clear and short.

questions.question: The Sanskrit word for 'interview' (face-to-face questioning) is ____.
questions.explanation: साक्षात्कारः = interview, one of the three source types.

questions.question: The Sanskrit word for 'field visit' (going to the place itself) is ____.
questions.explanation: क्षेत्र (place) + भ्रमणम् (touring) = field visit.

questions.question: The Sanskrit word for the 'outline' (form-line) of a report is ____.
questions.explanation: रूपरेखा = outline, the guide-map of the report.

questions.question: Complete: 'रूपरेखायाः अन्ते ____ भवति।' (At the end of the outline comes the bibliography.)
questions.explanation: The list of sources closes the outline.

questions.question: The Sanskrit word for the written 'report' of a project is ____.
questions.explanation: प्रतिवेदनम् = report.

questions.question: Complete: 'लेखनं शुद्धं ____ च भवेत्।' (The writing should be correct and simple.)
questions.explanation: सरलम् = simple; writing should be correct and simple.

questions.question: Complete: 'प्रस्तुतौ मन्दं ____ च वदेत्।' (In the presentation one should speak slowly and clearly.)
questions.explanation: स्पष्टम् = clearly.

questions.question: Complete: 'अन्तिमं सोपानं ____ अस्ति।' (The final step is evaluation.)
questions.explanation: मूल्याङ्कनम् (evaluation) is the sixth and last step.

questions.question: Fill the क्त्वा form of चि: 'विषयं ____ छात्रः सामग्रीं संगृह्णाति।' (Having chosen the topic, the student collects material.)
questions.explanation: चि + क्त्वा = चित्वा, 'having chosen'.

questions.question: Fill the क्त्वा form of लिख्: 'प्रतिवेदनं ____ सा प्रस्तुतिं करोति।' (Having written the report, she makes the presentation.)
questions.explanation: लिख् + क्त्वा = लिखित्वा, 'having written'.

questions.question: Complete the guiding line of the tree project: '____ फलन्ति वृक्षाः।' (Trees bear fruit for the good of others.)
questions.explanation: परोपकाराय = for the good of others (dative of purpose).

questions.question: What is a परियोजना? Break the word into its parts and explain its meaning in one or two sentences.
questions.answer: परियोजना = परि (around, thoroughly) + योजना (planning, from the root युज् 'to join'). It means a 'thorough plan' — a project: a piece of independent study in which the learner chooses a topic, gathers material, arranges it, writes a report and presents it.
questions.explanation: The etymology परि + योजना itself describes what a project is — planned, thorough work.

questions.question: Name the four abilities that project work builds, with their Sanskrit terms.
questions.answer: (1) स्वाध्यायः — independent study and reading of sources; (2) अनुसन्धानम् — inquiry: questioning, observing, interviewing; (3) लेखनकौशलम् — the skill of organised writing in simple Sanskrit; (4) प्रस्तुतिकौशलम् — the confidence and skill of presenting before a group.
questions.explanation: A project trains study, inquiry, writing and presentation together.

questions.question: Frame ONE suitable Sanskrit project topic connected with your own town or village, and show in one line that it meets the criteria of topic choice.
questions.answer: Example: 'मम नगरस्य उत्सवाः' (The festivals of my town). It is रुचिकर (I see these festivals myself), सीमित (one town, a few festivals), साधनसुलभ (elders and local temples are nearby sources) and संस्कृत-सम्बद्ध (festival names, mantras and customs involve Sanskrit).
questions.explanation: Any local, limited, source-rich, Sanskrit-related topic with the four criteria named is acceptable.

questions.question: A student proposes the topic 'भारतस्य सर्वाणि मन्दिराणि' (all the temples of India). Point out the problem and improve the topic.
questions.answer: The problem: the topic is अतिविस्तृत (far too broad) — no student can visit or describe all temples of India, and no clear outline is possible. Improvement: limit it to what is near and observable, e.g. 'मम ग्रामस्य मन्दिराणि' (the temples of my village) or 'मम नगरस्य प्रमुखं मन्दिरम्' (the chief temple of my town).
questions.explanation: Narrowing an over-broad topic to a local, bounded one is the standard fix.

questions.question: Give the meanings of these topic-choice terms: रुचिकरः, सीमितः, साधनसुलभः, शीर्षकम्.
questions.answer: रुचिकरः = interesting (to the student); सीमितः = limited/bounded, manageable; साधनसुलभः = having easily available sources/means; शीर्षकम् = the title (which should be short and clear).
questions.explanation: These four words carry the whole doctrine of topic selection.

questions.question: What is a प्रश्नावली and how is it used in a साक्षात्कारः?
questions.answer: A प्रश्नावली (प्रश्न + आवली, 'row of questions') is a prepared questionnaire — a short ordered list of questions written BEFORE the interview. During the साक्षात्कारः the student politely asks these questions to a knowledgeable person (priest, teacher, elder) and notes down the answers with the person's name and the date.
questions.explanation: Preparing questions in advance keeps the interview focused and its record citable.

questions.question: Write two simple Sanskrit questions (in Devanagari) that a student could ask the temple priest during a साक्षात्कारः for the temple project.
questions.answer: Examples: (1) एतत् मन्दिरं कदा निर्मितम्? (When was this temple built?) (2) अत्र कः उत्सवः प्रमुखः? (Which festival is the chief one here?) Other correct simple questions such as 'अस्य मन्दिरस्य देवता का?' (Who is the deity of this temple?) are equally acceptable.
questions.explanation: Interview questions should be short, polite and directly related to the project sections.

questions.question: What should a student DO during a क्षेत्रभ्रमणम् (field visit)? Mention at least three activities with their Sanskrit terms.
questions.answer: (1) निरीक्षणम् — observe the place and objects carefully; (2) टिप्पणी-लेखनम् — write short notes on the spot (and finish them the same day); (3) चित्रग्रहणम् — take photographs with permission; also record where and when each piece of information was found, for the सन्दर्भसूची.
questions.explanation: Observation, notes and photographs make first-hand material citable and reliable.

questions.question: What is विषयविभाजनम् and why is it done before writing the report?
questions.answer: विषयविभाजनम् is dividing the big topic into 4–6 small sections (अंशाः) and arranging them in a logical order — this ordered list is the रूपरेखा. It is done first because the outline works like a guide-map: it prevents repetition, keeps the writing in order, and shows at a glance which material is still missing.
questions.explanation: Division and ordering of the subject is the planning heart of the report.

questions.question: Construct a five-part रूपरेखा (in Sanskrit headings) for the project 'मम विद्यालयस्य पुस्तकालयः' (My school's library).
questions.answer: Example: (1) प्रस्तावना — विद्यालयस्य पुस्तकालयस्य परिचयः; (2) पुस्तकानां विवरणम् — कति पुस्तकानि, के विषयाः; (3) संस्कृतपुस्तकानि — कोशाः ग्रन्थाः च; (4) पुस्तकालयस्य उपयोगः — छात्राः कथं पठन्ति; (5) निष्कर्षः सन्दर्भसूची च। Any logical 4–6 part outline from introduction to conclusion and bibliography is acceptable.
questions.explanation: The outline must run from प्रस्तावना through ordered sections to निष्कर्षः and सन्दर्भसूची.

questions.question: Give the English meanings: प्रस्तावना, निष्कर्षः, सन्दर्भसूची, अंशः.
questions.answer: प्रस्तावना = introduction; निष्कर्षः = conclusion; सन्दर्भसूची = bibliography (list of sources); अंशः = a section/part (of the divided topic).
questions.explanation: These four terms name the skeleton of every project report.

questions.question: State any four qualities of good प्रतिवेदनलेखनम् (report writing) taught in this lesson.
questions.answer: Any four of: (1) it follows the रूपरेखा section by section; (2) the Sanskrit is simple and correct (शुद्धं सरलं च); (3) paragraphs are short, one section per heading; (4) tables, lists and pictures carry captions and numbers; (5) the प्रस्तावना states the aim and method, the निष्कर्षः states what was learnt; (6) it is revised (संशोधनम्) before submission.
questions.explanation: Order, simplicity, correctness and revision are the four pillars of the report.

questions.question: Write a two-sentence Sanskrit निष्कर्षः (conclusion) for the tree project 'पर्यावरणसंरक्षणे वृक्षाणां महत्त्वम्', and give its English meaning.
questions.answer: Example: वृक्षाः छायां फलं शुद्धवायुं च ददति, अतः ते पर्यावरणस्य रक्षकाः सन्ति। वयं सर्वे प्रतिवर्षं वृक्षान् रोपयेम। (Trees give shade, fruit and pure air; therefore they are the protectors of the environment. May we all plant trees every year.) Any correct simple two-sentence conclusion stating the finding and a resolve is acceptable.
questions.explanation: A conclusion states what was found and what should be done.

questions.question: Why should a student read the finished report aloud once before submitting it?
questions.answer: Because the ear catches errors the eye misses: wrong sandhi, missing case endings and clumsy sentences become audible when read aloud. Reading aloud is therefore a simple, effective part of संशोधनम् (revision) before submission.
questions.explanation: An aural check complements the visual proofreading of spelling and grammar.

questions.question: List four features of a good प्रस्तुतिः (presentation) as taught in the lesson.
questions.answer: (1) Tell the essence (सारः) of the project in a few minutes — do not read the whole report; (2) speak slowly and clearly (मन्दं स्पष्टं च वदेत्); (3) show the main points on a chart (सूचनापटः) or slides and recite a Sanskrit line or two; (4) answer the listeners' questions politely.
questions.explanation: Essence, clarity, visual support and courteous answers make the presentation.

questions.question: Give the two Sanskrit self-evaluation questions from the lesson and their English meanings.
questions.answer: (1) किम् उद्देश्यं सिद्धम्? — Was the aim achieved? (2) किं सर्वे स्रोताः निर्दिष्टाः? — Are all sources cited? The student asks these of his or her own work before submission.
questions.explanation: Self-evaluation precedes the teacher's मूल्याङ्कनम्.

questions.question: Two projects on the same topic are submitted. Project A copies three pages from a book neatly; Project B has a short outline, its own simple Sanskrit sentences, an interview record and a source list. Which deserves the higher evaluation and why?
questions.answer: Project B. Evaluation rewards मौलिकता (originality), variety and honesty of sources, order of the outline, and one's own correct language. Project A, however neat, is प्रतिलिपिः (mere copying) without inquiry, so it fails the chief criteria; Project B shows real अनुसन्धानम् — its own words, an interview and cited sources.
questions.explanation: Originality with cited sources outweighs neat copying.

questions.question: Give the Sanskrit process terms for: selection, collection, division, writing, presentation, evaluation.
questions.answer: Selection = चयनम्; collection = संग्रहः; division = विभाजनम्; writing = लेखनम्; presentation = प्रस्तुतिः; evaluation = मूल्याङ्कनम्.
questions.explanation: These six words name the six steps of the project process.

questions.question: Translate into Sanskrit using a क्त्वा/ल्यप् form: 'Having collected the material, the student composes the outline.' Then name the form you used.
questions.answer: सामग्रीं संगृह्य छात्रः रूपरेखां रचयति। The form संगृह्य is the ल्यप् (gerund) of सम् + ग्रह् — used instead of क्त्वा because the root has a prefix; it means 'having collected'.
questions.explanation: Prefixed roots take ल्यप् (-य): संगृह्य; unprefixed roots take क्त्वा: चित्वा, लिखित्वा.

questions.question: State the aim (उद्देश्यम्) of the model project 'संस्कृतसुभाषितसंग्रहः' and its two main working methods.
questions.answer: Aim: विषयानुसारं पञ्चविंशतिः सुभाषितानां संग्रहः अर्थलेखनं च — to collect 25 subhashitas theme-wise and write their meanings. Methods: (1) library work with books of subhashitas as the chief source; (2) वर्गीकरणम् — classifying the verses by theme (विद्या, उद्यम, सदाचार) and writing each verse's meaning in simple Sanskrit and English.
questions.explanation: This model shows a book-based, classification-centred project.

questions.question: Compare the sources of 'मम ग्रामस्य मन्दिराणि' and 'संस्कृतसुभाषितसंग्रहः'. How do they differ?
questions.answer: The temple project rests mainly on first-hand sources: क्षेत्रभ्रमणम् (visits to the temples) and साक्षात्कारः (interviews with the priest and elders), since little is written about local temples. The subhashita project rests mainly on written sources: ग्रन्थाः in the library, with the work being collection and theme-wise classification. Thus one is field-and-interview based, the other book-based.
questions.explanation: The topic decides the source mix — local heritage needs the field; verse collection needs books.

questions.question: List any four common project mistakes (सामान्यदोषाः) named in the lesson.
questions.answer: Any four of: (1) choosing an over-broad topic (अतिविस्तृतः विषयः); (2) copying from books without understanding (प्रतिलिपिः) instead of writing in one's own words with citation; (3) writing without a रूपरेखा, causing disorder and repetition; (4) omitting the सन्दर्भसूची; (5) skipping revision (संशोधनम्); (6) reading the whole report aloud in the presentation.
questions.explanation: Knowing the standard failures is half the craft of avoiding them.

questions.question: Explain the six steps (षट् सोपानानि) of परियोजना-निर्माणम् in order, writing one or two sentences on what is done at each step.
questions.answer: (1) विषयचयनम् — choose a topic that is interesting, limited, source-rich and Sanskrit-related, and give it a short clear title. (2) सामग्रीसंग्रहः — collect material from books (ग्रन्थाः), interviews (साक्षात्कारः with a प्रश्नावली) and field visits (क्षेत्रभ्रमणम्), recording every source. (3) विषयविभाजनम्/रूपरेखा — divide the topic into 4–6 ordered sections and fix the outline from प्रस्तावना to सन्दर्भसूची. (4) प्रतिवेदनलेखनम् — write the report in simple correct Sanskrit following the outline, then revise it. (5) प्रस्तुतिः — present the essence of the project clearly with a chart or slides and answer questions. (6) मूल्याङ्कनम् — the project is evaluated on originality, sources, order, language, neatness and presentation, after the student's own self-check.
questions.explanation: The six steps form one connected journey from choosing to evaluating.

questions.question: 'A well-chosen topic is half the project.' Discuss this statement using the four criteria of विषयचयनम्, giving one example of a good topic and one of a bad topic with reasons.
questions.answer: Topic choice decides everything that follows — what sources are needed, whether an outline can be made, and whether the project can be finished. The four criteria: रुचिकरः (interest keeps the student working), सीमितः (a limited scope can actually be covered), साधनसुलभः (sources must be reachable — books, people, places nearby), संस्कृत-सम्बद्धः (the topic must belong to Sanskrit language or culture). Good example: 'मम ग्रामस्य मन्दिराणि' — local, bounded, observable, with a priest to interview; the outline almost writes itself. Bad example: 'संस्कृतसाहित्यम्' — अतिविस्तृतः; no student can cover all of Sanskrit literature, sources are endless, no clear division is possible, so the report becomes vague copying. Hence a well-chosen topic truly is half the project: with it the remaining five steps flow naturally; without it they all stall.
questions.explanation: Each criterion links directly to the feasibility of the later steps.

questions.question: Describe the three kinds of sources for सामग्रीसंग्रहः — ग्रन्थाः, साक्षात्कारः and क्षेत्रभ्रमणम् — explaining for each: what it is, what tools it needs, and one precaution to observe.
questions.answer: (1) ग्रन्थाः — written sources: textbooks, dictionaries (शब्दकोशाः), collections of verses, magazines and reliable web pages. Tools: reading notes and a list of titles, authors and page numbers. Precaution: never copy blindly; understand, write in your own words and record each book for the सन्दर्भसूची. (2) साक्षात्कारः — the interview: face-to-face questioning of knowledgeable people (priest, teacher, elders). Tools: a prepared प्रश्नावली and a notebook for answers. Precaution: be polite, ask short clear questions, and note the person's name and the date. (3) क्षेत्रभ्रमणम् — the field visit: going to the place itself (temple, river bank, library) to observe. Tools: टिप्पणी (on-the-spot notes) and, with permission, photographs. Precaution: record where and when each observation was made, and complete the notes the same day so nothing is forgotten.
questions.explanation: Books, interviews and field visits each demand their own tools and discipline.

questions.question: Take the topic 'मम नगरस्य नदी' (The river of my town). Divide it into sections and write a complete six-part रूपरेखा with Sanskrit headings, then explain in English why your order is logical.
questions.answer: Example रूपरेखा: (1) प्रस्तावना — नद्याः नाम स्थानं च; (2) नद्याः स्वरूपम् — उद्गमः मार्गः च; (3) नदीतीरस्य जीवनम् — कृषिः घट्टाः उत्सवाः च; (4) संस्कृतवाङ्मये नद्यः — नदीविषयकाणि वचनानि; (5) नद्याः संरक्षणम् — समस्याः उपायाः च; (6) निष्कर्षः सन्दर्भसूची च। The order is logical because it moves from introduction (what and where the river is), to description (its form), to human life around it, then to its place in Sanskrit literature, then to the problem of protecting it, and finally to the conclusion with sources — each section prepares the reader for the next, and nothing is repeated.
questions.explanation: A good outline moves from the general to the particular and ends in conclusion and citation.

questions.question: Write a short Sanskrit प्रस्तावना (3–4 sentences, in Devanagari) for the project 'मम ग्रामस्य मन्दिराणि', stating the aim and the method. Give the English meaning.
questions.answer: Example: मम ग्रामे त्रीणि मन्दिराणि सन्ति। अस्याः परियोजनायाः उद्देश्यं तेषां मन्दिराणां परिचयः संस्कृतेन लेखनम् च अस्ति। अहं क्षेत्रभ्रमणं कृत्वा पुरोहितस्य साक्षात्कारं च कृत्वा सामग्रीम् असंगृह्णम्। अन्ते निष्कर्षं सन्दर्भसूचीं च लिखामि। (In my village there are three temples. The aim of this project is to introduce those temples and write about them in Sanskrit. I collected the material by making field visits and interviewing the priest. At the end I write the conclusion and the bibliography.) Any correct simple introduction stating aim and method is acceptable.
questions.explanation: A प्रस्तावना must state उद्देश्यम् (aim) and विधिः (method) in simple correct Sanskrit.

questions.question: Prepare an evaluation checklist of six points for judging a Sanskrit project, and explain briefly how a student can use the same checklist for self-evaluation before submission.
questions.answer: Checklist: (1) विषयः — is the topic well-chosen and original (मौलिकता)? (2) स्रोतांसि — are the sources varied (books, interview, field visit) and all cited in the सन्दर्भसूची? (3) रूपरेखा — is the outline complete and logically ordered from प्रस्तावना to निष्कर्षः? (4) भाषा — is the Sanskrit simple and correct in spelling, sandhi and विभक्ति? (5) स्वच्छता — are pages, sections and pictures numbered, neat and captioned? (6) प्रस्तुतिः — was the essence presented clearly and were questions answered? For self-evaluation the student walks the same list BEFORE submission, asking किम् उद्देश्यं सिद्धम्? and किं सर्वे स्रोताः निर्दिष्टाः?, marking each point yes/no and repairing every 'no' — re-ordering sections, adding missing citations, correcting language — so the evaluator later finds nothing lacking.
questions.explanation: The same six criteria serve the teacher's judgement and the student's self-check.

questions.question: Write five connected Sanskrit sentences (in Devanagari) narrating a student's whole project journey, using at least three of these forms: चित्वा, संगृह्य, लिखित्वा, संग्रहीतुम्, प्रस्तुतौ. Give the English meaning of each sentence.
questions.answer: Example: 1. रमेशः 'मम ग्रामस्य मन्दिराणि' इति विषयं चित्वा शीर्षकम् अलिखत्। (Having chosen the topic 'the temples of my village', Ramesh wrote the title.) 2. सामग्रीं संग्रहीतुं सः मन्दिराणि अगच्छत् पुरोहितं च अपृच्छत्। (To collect material he went to the temples and questioned the priest.) 3. सामग्रीं संगृह्य सः षड्भागां रूपरेखाम् अरचयत्। (Having collected the material, he composed a six-part outline.) 4. ततः प्रतिवेदनं लिखित्वा सः एकवारं संशोधनम् अकरोत्। (Then, having written the report, he revised it once.) 5. प्रस्तुतौ सः मन्दं स्पष्टं च अवदत्, प्रश्नानाम् उत्तराणि च अददात्। (In the presentation he spoke slowly and clearly, and gave answers to the questions.)
questions.explanation: क्त्वा/ल्यप्, तुमुन् and सप्तमी forms knit the six steps into a flowing narrative.

questions.question: Compare the three model projects — 'मम ग्रामस्य मन्दिराणि', 'संस्कृतसुभाषितसंग्रहः' and 'पर्यावरणसंरक्षणे वृक्षाणां महत्त्वम्' — under three heads: aim, main sources, and the special skill each one trains.
questions.answer: (1) मम ग्रामस्य मन्दिराणि — Aim: to introduce and describe the village temples in Sanskrit. Main sources: क्षेत्रभ्रमणम् (visits to the temples) and साक्षात्कारः (priest and elders); books play a small part. Special skill: observation and description — turning what is seen and heard into simple Sanskrit sentences. (2) संस्कृतसुभाषितसंग्रहः — Aim: to collect 25 subhashitas theme-wise with meanings. Main source: ग्रन्थाः in the library. Special skill: वर्गीकरणम् (classification) and translation — grouping verses by theme and rendering their sense. (3) पर्यावरणसंरक्षणे वृक्षाणां महत्त्वम् — Aim: to describe the benefits of trees and inspire tree-planting. Sources: books joined with a field count of trees near the school. Special skill: combining textual study with survey data and ending in an action plan (वृक्षारोपणयोजना). Together they show that the SAME six-step method fits a field project, a library project and a mixed study-action project.
questions.explanation: The three models illustrate field-based, book-based and mixed project designs under one method.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
सीता दशमकक्षायाः छात्रा अस्ति। सा परियोजनां कर्तुम् इच्छति, किन्तु सा चिन्तयति — 'अहं प्रथमं किं करोमि? किं प्रथमं प्रतिवेदनं लिखामि?' तस्याः अध्यापिका वदति — 'न हि! प्रथमं विषयं चिनु, ततः सामग्रीं संगृहाण, ततः रूपरेखां रचय, ततः एव लिख।'
Questions: (a) What does Sita want to do? (b) What mistake was Sita about to make? (c) State, in order, the three steps the teacher asks her to complete BEFORE writing.
questions.answer: (a) Sita wants to make a project (परियोजना). (b) She was about to write the report FIRST, skipping all the earlier steps. (c) The teacher tells her: first choose the topic (विषयं चिनु — विषयचयनम्), then collect the material (सामग्रीं संगृहाण — सामग्रीसंग्रहः), then compose the outline (रूपरेखां रचय) — and only then write (ततः एव लिख).
questions.explanation: The case tests the fixed order of the project steps: choose, collect, outline, then write.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
चत्वारः छात्राः विषयान् प्रस्तुवन्ति। रामः वदति — 'मम विषयः विश्वस्य सर्वाणि काव्यानि।' श्यामा वदति — 'मम विषयः मम ग्रामस्य कृषकाणां लोकोक्तयः।' गोपालः वदति — 'मम विषयः चन्द्रयानम्।' राधा वदति — 'मम विषयः मम विद्यालयस्य संस्कृतदिनोत्सवः।'
Questions: (a) Which two topics are suitable for a Sanskrit project and why? (b) Why is Rama's topic unsuitable? (c) Why is Gopala's topic unsuitable?
questions.answer: (a) Shyama's ('the sayings/proverbs of my village farmers') and Radha's ('my school's Sanskrit-day festival') are suitable: both are सीमित (limited), साधनसुलभ (people and events are nearby to observe and interview), रुचिकर and संस्कृत-सम्बद्ध. (b) Rama's 'all the poems of the world' is अतिविस्तृत — impossibly broad; no outline or complete collection is possible. (c) Gopala's 'Chandrayaan' is not संस्कृत-सम्बद्ध — it is a space-science topic with no connection to Sanskrit language or culture, however interesting it may be.
questions.explanation: Applying the four criteria separates workable topics from broad or unrelated ones.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
मोहनः 'मम ग्रामस्य मन्दिराणि' इति परियोजनां करोति। सः रविवासरे मन्दिरं गत्वा निरीक्षणम् अकरोत्, टिप्पणीः अलिखत्, अनुमतिं गृहीत्वा चित्राणि च अगृह्णात्। ततः सः पुरोहितं प्रश्नावल्या अपृच्छत् — 'मन्दिरं कदा निर्मितम्? कः उत्सवः प्रमुखः?' गृहं आगत्य सः सर्वं सङ्ग्रहपुस्तके अलिखत्।
Questions: (a) Which TWO kinds of sources did Mohan use? (b) Name three correct field-work habits shown in the passage. (c) Which of the three source types did Mohan NOT use here?
questions.answer: (a) He used क्षेत्रभ्रमणम् (a field visit to the temple) and साक्षात्कारः (interviewing the priest with a questionnaire). (b) Correct habits: he observed carefully (निरीक्षणम्), wrote notes on the spot (टिप्पणीः), took photographs only after taking permission (अनुमतिं गृहीत्वा), used a prepared प्रश्नावली, and wrote everything in his collection-book the same day — any three. (c) He did not use ग्रन्थाः (books/written sources) in this passage.
questions.explanation: The case shows model field-visit and interview practice, with books still to be consulted.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
लता स्वपरियोजनार्थं जालपुटात् (from a website) पञ्च पृष्ठानि मुद्रयित्वा प्रतिवेदने अयोजयत्। सा न किमपि स्रोतः अलिखत्, न च स्वशब्दैः किमपि अलिखत्। अध्यापकः अवदत् — 'एषा प्रतिलिपिः अस्ति, न अनुसन्धानम्।'
Questions: (a) What two mistakes did Lata make? (b) Why does the teacher call her work 'प्रतिलिपिः, not अनुसन्धानम्'? (c) What should she do to correct it?
questions.answer: (a) She copied printed pages directly into her report without writing anything in her own words, and she cited no source (no सन्दर्भसूची entry). (b) Because merely reproducing another's pages shows no inquiry of her own — no questioning, understanding or expression; copying is प्रतिलिपिः, while अनुसन्धानम् means finding out and stating things oneself. (c) She should read the material, understand it, write the matter in her own simple Sanskrit, and list the website (with its name and date of access) in the सन्दर्भसूची — using it as a cited source, not as the report itself.
questions.explanation: The case dramatises the copying mistake and its remedy: own words plus honest citation.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
गीता 'संस्कृतसुभाषितसंग्रहः' इति परियोजनायाः रूपरेखां रचयति — (१) प्रस्तावना; (२) विद्याविषयकाणि सुभाषितानि; (३) उद्यमविषयकाणि सुभाषितानि; (४) सदाचारविषयकाणि सुभाषितानि; (५) निष्कर्षः। तस्याः मित्रं वदति — 'एकः अंशः न्यूनः अस्ति!'
Questions: (a) On what principle has Gita divided her middle sections? (b) Which essential part is missing from her outline? (c) Where should it be added?
questions.answer: (a) She has divided the middle theme-wise (विषयानुसारम् / वर्गीकरणम्): verses on knowledge, on effort, on good conduct. (b) The सन्दर्भसूची (bibliography — the list of books from which the verses were collected) is missing. (c) It should be added at the very end, after the निष्कर्षः — the standard outline runs प्रस्तावना → sections → निष्कर्षः → सन्दर्भसूची.
questions.explanation: The case checks knowledge of the complete standard outline and theme-wise division.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
अर्जुनः स्वप्रतिवेदनम् एकस्मिन् एव रात्रौ अलिखत्। सः संशोधनं न अकरोत्। प्रतिवेदने बहवः दोषाः आसन् — 'छात्रः पठति' इति स्थाने 'छात्रः पठती' इति, 'मन्दिरे' इति स्थाने 'मन्दिरः' इति च लिखितम्। चित्राणां अधः किमपि नाम न आसीत्।
Questions: (a) Which step of report writing did Arjuna skip? (b) What kinds of language errors appear in his report? (c) What rule about pictures did he break? (d) What habit would have prevented all this?
questions.answer: (a) He skipped संशोधनम् (revision) — he wrote in one night and submitted the first draft. (b) Language errors of form and case: a wrong verb form ('पठती' for पठति) and a wrong विभक्ति/form ('मन्दिरः' where the locative मन्दिरे is needed) — that is, errors of spelling and case endings. (c) His pictures had no captions (and no numbers) beneath them. (d) Starting early and revising at least once — reading the draft aloud and checking spelling, sandhi and case endings — would have caught these faults.
questions.explanation: The case shows why revision and captioning are non-negotiable parts of प्रतिवेदनलेखनम्.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
कक्षायां द्वे प्रस्तुती अभवताम्। मीना विंशतिपृष्ठात्मकं प्रतिवेदनं शीघ्रं शीघ्रम् अपठत्; श्रोतारः किमपि न अवगच्छन्। कमला तु सूचनापटे मुख्यबिन्दून् अदर्शयत्, मन्दं स्पष्टं च सारम् अवदत्, एकं सुभाषितं च अपाठयत्, प्रश्नानाम् उत्तराणि च अददात्।
Questions: (a) What mistakes did Meena make? (b) Name three good presentation practices shown by Kamala. (c) Whose presentation would score higher in मूल्याङ्कनम् and why?
questions.answer: (a) Meena read the whole twenty-page report aloud, and she read it fast — so the listeners understood nothing; she did not present the essence. (b) Kamala showed the main points on a chart (सूचनापटः), spoke the essence slowly and clearly (मन्दं स्पष्टं च), recited a subhashita, and answered the audience's questions — any three. (c) Kamala's — because evaluation of the प्रस्तुतिः rewards clarity, essence-telling, visual support and question-handling, all of which she showed and Meena did not.
questions.explanation: The contrast case fixes the rule: present the essence clearly; never read the whole report.

questions.question:
Read the sentence and answer:
'विषयं चित्वा, ग्रन्थेभ्यः सामग्रीं संगृह्य, छात्रा प्रश्नावल्या साक्षात्कारं कृत्वा, प्रतिवेदनं लिखित्वा, प्रस्तुतौ सारम् अवदत्।'
Questions: (a) List the four gerund (क्त्वा/ल्यप्) forms in the sentence and give their meanings. (b) State the विभक्ति and role of ग्रन्थेभ्यः, प्रश्नावल्या and प्रस्तुतौ.
questions.answer: (a) चित्वा = having chosen; संगृह्य = having collected (ल्यप्, because सम्+ग्रह् has a prefix); कृत्वा = having done/made; लिखित्वा = having written. (b) ग्रन्थेभ्यः — पञ्चमी (ablative) plural: 'from the books', the source; प्रश्नावल्या — तृतीया (instrumental): 'with the questionnaire', the means; प्रस्तुतौ — सप्तमी (locative): 'in the presentation', the place/occasion.
questions.explanation: One sentence carries the whole grammar of the chapter: gerund chains plus the three key cases.

questions.question:
Read the outline and answer:
कश्चित् छात्रः इमां रूपरेखां रचितवान् — शीर्षकम्: 'पर्यावरणसंरक्षणे वृक्षाणां महत्त्वम्'। (१) प्रस्तावना — पर्यावरणसमस्या; (२) वृक्षाणाम् उपकाराः; (३) संस्कृतवाङ्मये वृक्षाः; (४) विद्यालयपरिसरस्य वृक्षाणां सूची; (५) वृक्षारोपणयोजना; (६) निष्कर्षः सन्दर्भसूची च।
Questions: (a) Which section requires field work, and what field activity does it involve? (b) Which section connects the project to Sanskrit literature? (c) Which section turns the project into action? (d) Which Sanskrit line would fittingly guide this project?
questions.answer: (a) Section 4 (विद्यालयपरिसरस्य वृक्षाणां सूची) requires field work — counting and listing the trees of the school campus by direct observation (क्षेत्रनिरीक्षणम्). (b) Section 3 (संस्कृतवाङ्मये वृक्षाः) — sayings about trees in Sanskrit literature. (c) Section 5 (वृक्षारोपणयोजना) — the tree-planting plan turns study into action. (d) परोपकाराय फलन्ति वृक्षाः — 'trees bear fruit for the good of others'.
questions.explanation: The case tests reading a model outline and matching sections to source types and purposes.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
विनोदः 'मम ग्रामस्य मन्दिराणि' इति परियोजनार्थं गृहे एव उपविश्य एकस्मात् पुरातत्त्वग्रन्थात् अन्यनगरस्य मन्दिराणां वर्णनम् अलिखत्। सः स्वग्रामस्य मन्दिरं न अगच्छत्, न च कमपि अपृच्छत्।
Questions: (a) What is wrong with Vinod's method for THIS topic? (b) Which two source types has he ignored, and why are they essential here? (c) Suggest two concrete corrections.
questions.answer: (a) His material does not match his topic: he copied a book's description of ANOTHER town's temples while his project is about his own village's temples — sitting at home, he collected nothing about his actual subject. (b) He ignored क्षेत्रभ्रमणम् (field visits) and साक्षात्कारः (interviews) — essential here because local temples are not described in books; only visiting them and questioning the priest and elders can supply true first-hand material. (c) Corrections: visit each village temple, observe and write टिप्पणीः (and photograph with permission); interview the पुरोहित and elders with a prepared प्रश्नावली — and then use books only as supporting, cited sources in the सन्दर्भसूची.
questions.explanation: The case tests matching sources to topic: a local field topic cannot be done from a distant book.
